note: Daily council 2026-08-09. PRE-REGISTRATION, committed before any result exists. SELECTION AND COLLISION CHECKS RUN AT 2026-08-09T11:14:51Z, at session open, BEFORE this file was written or committed (0807-O7: a pasted repository fact must be labelled with when it was run, because it is not reproducible at its own commit). `sorted(glob('analytics/fetch-requests/*.json'))[-1]` returned 2026-08-08-daily.json; with this filename appended it returns 2026-08-09-daily.json, so this batch is the one newest_request() will select despite the lexicographic-not-mtime defect (propose-only since 2026-08-05, still unfixed at session open). `ls analytics/fetch-results/ | grep -c 2026-08-09` returned 0: no name collision. SIX ROWS IN THREE GROUPS. This batch is the 2026-08-08 close-out's next step 1 — the analyst's proposal 5 amended by his proposal 1 (the same-host positive control BRACKETS the substantive rows, fired both first and last, so a late host-wide transient is excluded rather than assumed away) — plus next step 3, the route-admissibility pre-flight adopted yesterday as the day's one optimization item. PRE-FLIGHT CHECK RUN: every (outcome, status-class) pair below maps to a named branch, and each group's uninformative branch is named explicitly rather than left to be read through a neighbouring clause. GROUP A — THE BRACKETED HALF-FACTORIAL on the identification residual left open by ruling 0804-B7, untouched for three days. Rows 1 and 6 are the SAME URL (true id 978, true slug) fired first and last; row 4 is the false-id/true-slug cell (999999, china---switzerland-bit-2009-). THIS BATCH CANNOT CLOSE THE RESIDUAL AND IS NOT DESIGNED TO: it fires ONE of the two false-id cells by the analyst's own design, so it is a HALF-FACTORIAL by construction, and branch 2d of 2026-08-08 governs — a 2x2 missing a cell does not become a 1x2 that happens to agree with us. The most a favourable result buys today is one half; the other half is fired tomorrow under the same bracketing, and only with both halves in may the residual close. A further weakening is named here in advance rather than discovered later: the true-id/FALSE-slug 200 sits at 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-08, not today, so any completed factorial will be assembled ACROSS DATES, and cross-date assembly of a factorial is weaker than a within-batch one. GROUP B — THE COMMISSION PAGE GETS ITS FIRST SAME-PAGE POSITIVE CONTROL, and this is the substantive question of the day. For eight days this council has read a find_matched:false on A/81/17 at uncitral.un.org/en/commission as a null about publication. That page has NEVER carried a positive control: nobody has established that its rendered text carries ANY session-report symbol. Row 3 asks the page for A/80/17 — the fifty-eighth session's report, known to the record as published and named in the 2026-08-08 memo section 6 as a returned search title. Row 2 asks the same page for A/81/17. If the page does not carry A/80/17 either, then every prior null on this surface was uninformative about publication and the surface must be retired for symbol-existence purposes — a RETROACTIVE state change, which is why the control is fired before another day's null is banked. GROUP C — ROUTE-ADMISSIBILITY PRE-FLIGHT. Row 5 is digitallibrary.un.org/robots.txt. On 2026-08-08 three of seven rows were spent discovering that this project's OWN robots compliance closes digitallibrary.un.org/search to it; one row on the policy file would have returned that fact AND the rules around it. This row does not re-fire /search (next step 2 forbids it: the disallow is deterministic given a stable robots.txt, so a repeat is not a retry but the same non-observation at a second cost) and it is NOT discovery — it retrieves a policy file about a host already on the allowlist and already used, and it requests no unknown item. Yesterday's two caveats are carried as conditions, not decoration: a robots.txt row is itself subject to the same robots check and to the fail-open path in src/sources/base.py, so a null on it is uninformative in exactly the way 2026-08-08's Group 1 was; and the 400-character excerpt cannot carry a long rules file, so the row establishes REACHABILITY and the HEAD OF THE FILE, never the full policy. Every row carries a non-empty find, continuing the correction of the 0807-B5 three-state find_matched defect; the relay-generated control row still cannot be reached by a request-file fix and will again record find_matched:false having asked nothing (0808-C9, propose-only). DECISION RULES, FIXED IN ADVANCE. GROUP A: (P0-OPEN) row 1 must return outcome 'ok', HTTP 200, find_matched true. (P0-CLOSE) row 6 must return outcome 'ok', HTTP 200, find_matched true. If EITHER bracket row fails, the batch is UNINFORMATIVE FOR investmentpolicy.unctad.org, no branch is entered, and no discharge is claimed either way — this is the whole point of bracketing and it is not to be softened after the fact. (A1) If both brackets hold and row 4 returns 200 with find_matched true, the head tracks the URL SLUG irrespective of the numeric id, and the 0804-B7 discharge REOPENS at slug level. This is the branch that costs us and it is named before the result exists. (A2) If both brackets hold and row 4 returns 404 or 410, or a final_url differing from the requested URL, the false-id/TRUE-SLUG half enters the id-is-load-bearing reading. NO CLOSURE IS CLAIMED TODAY: the false-id/false-slug half is unfired, so the factorial remains incomplete under branch 2d, and it is re-fired tomorrow with the same bracketing. (A3) If row 4 returns a 5xx, it enters NO BRANCH. It is recorded only as further evidence that id 999999 errors stably — this would be its fourth separated timestamp — and per METHODOLOGY section 2.7's own table a 5xx remains uninformative about head generation. (A4) Any other non-'ok' outcome on row 4 — refused 403 or 429, refused other non-200, no_contact, no_client, robots_disallowed, not_attempted, scheme_not_https, private_address, host_not_allowed — is UNINFORMATIVE for that row and no conclusion is drawn from it. GROUP B: (P0-B) row 3 (A/80/17) must return outcome 'ok', HTTP 200, find_matched TRUE. (B0) If row 3 returns 'ok'/200 with find_matched FALSE, then this surface's rendered text does not carry a session-report symbol even for a report the record already holds as published, and EVERY prior A/81/17 null on this page is retroactively UNINFORMATIVE ABOUT PUBLICATION. The surface is retired for symbol-existence purposes with that reason recorded, open thread 3 is annotated, and this is escalated rather than banked. The competing explanation is pre-registered so it cannot be reached for afterwards: the page may list only current or forthcoming sessions, in which case the absence of A/80/17 is a property of the page's scope rather than of its rendering. BOTH readings yield the same operative conclusion at the reduction level — this surface does not answer the symbol question — and NEITHER is a statement about what the United Nations has or has not published. (B1) If P0-B holds (row 3 find_matched TRUE) and row 2 returns find_matched FALSE, that is the FIRST VALIDATED NULL on this surface in nine days: the symbol is absent from the rendered text of a page demonstrated in the same batch to carry the analogous prior symbol. It is recorded as 'not found in accessible sources at this instant', never as 'does not exist', per the cross-BIT consistency rule. (B2) If P0-B holds and row 2 returns find_matched TRUE, that is a POSITIVE and a state change. It is NOT to be asserted as publication on this datum alone: it is escalated, and confirmed by retrieving the record page itself in a later batch before any claim is made or any confidence cell moves. (B3) Any outcome other than 'ok' on row 2 or row 3 renders GROUP B UNINFORMATIVE ENTIRE, and if it strikes only one of them the other is still not read alone. (B-OBS, an observation and not a branch) Rows 2 and 3 are expected to return bytes 832338 and sha256 ca87a113c024605c..., the single byte length and single digest returned by all 19 'ok' fetches of this URL across 10 batch instants at origin scope (ruled 2026-08-08). A DIFFERING byte length or digest is the first change ever observed in this page and is to be reported as such — but per the same ruling it is a statement about the representation, not about any document, and it enters no branch. GROUP C: (C1) If row 5 returns 'ok'/200 with find_matched true, the excerpt carries the head of the policy that closed /search to this client; the paths it names are recorded as an ADMISSIBILITY MAP, explicitly bounded to the first 400 characters and not read as the full policy. (C2) If row 5 returns 'ok'/200 with find_matched FALSE, the file was reached and contains no 'Disallow:' token in it, which CONTRADICTS the 2026-08-08 robots_disallowed outcome; that inconsistency is escalated and NOT resolved silently or by reasoning. (C3) If row 5 itself returns robots_disallowed, this client forbids itself the policy file; that is recorded as an instrument fact and the row is uninformative. (C4) Any other non-'ok' outcome is uninformative. STANDING CONSTRAINT ON GROUP C, restated because it sits close to the cardinal rule: nothing in row 5 is a claim about the UN Digital Library's holdings, and the UN Digital Library RECORD route remains UNTESTED and is not to be recorded as tried — reaching it needs a record id the project does not hold, and obtaining one would be discovery, which the relay is not (analytics/fetch-requests/README.md, METHODOLOGY Part VIII). NOT FIRED TODAY: digitallibrary.un.org/search, per next step 2 of the 2026-08-08 close-out; the false-id/false-slug cell, deliberately held for tomorrow's bracketed batch; and Huawei ARB/22/2 (ICSID), a STANDING WEEKLY row adopted 2026-08-06 whose next firing is dated 2026-08-13 — a schedule set by the council is not re-opened because rows are cheap.
